title: feat(runtime): the MCP draft door answers a metadata type's contract
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DDxdrYJq965rUfrZBso8FS3)_
Fixes #35761
Clause-②: yes — widening: one new read on the draft door behind the same `metadata:write` grant and `manage_metadata` check; no save, publish or existing read changes, so nothing accepted today is refused.
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：通过 MCP 搭建应用的外部 AI 客户端，保存草稿前能读到某类元数据（如对象、视图、流程）允许写哪些字段、哪些必填和一份新建起步模板；默认只给精简版，需要细节时再按字段逐层展开，每次回复都控制在客户端读得下的大小之内；Studio 用户无感。
- 为什么做：属于 MCP 搭建主线；第一轮的完整规则对对象、视图这类最常写的类型太大（几十万字节），客户端读不进去，这一轮把它压到上限之内。
- 出错会怎样：只影响客户端主动要求读取规则的那次列表调用，保存和发布规则都不变；可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：本改动包含对外发布的技能说明，按人合档落地，需要你批准后合并。

## Round 2 (L1 C1)

L1-a found the contract reply too large for the types a door-only client writes most (comment 7043023208). The seat confirmed route (a), shape the reply, and that the PR stays `Fixes #35761`. This round:

- **`contract: true` now answers a lean contract by default**: a one-level projection of the same served schema, never a second hand-written shape. It carries the type's `required` keys and, for each top-level key, its `type` (a union as `a | b`, an array of scalars as `string[]`), `const`, an `enum` cut to 20 values (`enumTotal` then gives the count), a description cut to one line of at most 160 characters, and `drill`, the JSON Pointer of a key with nested structure. `createSeed` is kept. A schema whose root is a union (`view`) lists each alternative's own top-level keys the same way.
- **`contractPath`**, a JSON Pointer into the served schema, answers the full sub-schema at that pointer, verbatim (`form: "full"`). A sub-schema over the cap is answered in its lean form with `truncated: true` and a note, so the client drills again with one of its `drill` pointers. A `$ref` names its target in `drill` (`/$defs/...`).
- **Refusals, all `VALIDATION_ERROR 400`, before any protocol read where the input alone decides**: `contractPath` without `contract: true`; a `contractPath` that is not a JSON Pointer; a pointer that does not resolve, whose message names the pointer, the deepest point that resolved, the keys there, and the type's top-level keys; and a `contractPath` on a type with no schema, whose message carries the no-schema reason. A missing path is never answered with an empty schema.
- **Byte cap `CONTRACT_REPLY_BYTE_CAP` = 24 KiB (24,576 bytes)**, measured as the pretty-printed `{ contract }` the door answers. Why that number: MCP clients commonly cap one tool result near 25,000 tokens (Claude Code's default), and JSON dense with punctuation tokenizes at about two bytes per token at worst, so a capped contract stays near half that budget and leaves the rest for the item list it rides with. Every answer is tried richest first (full, then lean with descriptions, then lean without descriptions, then union alternatives by one descriptor each) and the first that fits is sent; if none fits, the answer is `schema: null` with a reason that names a narrower path. No contract above the cap is ever sent.

### Bytes per skill-table type, head 79ef0a142

Measured through the registry's own `list_metadata_items` reply, over the listing `getMetaTypes` serves for `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` (the served schemas, from the protocol's one converter). "Full" is `{ contract: { schema, createSeed } }` pretty-printed, which is what round 1 answered; "lean" is what this head answers for `contract: true` with no `contractPath`.

| type | served schema, compact JSON (characters) | full contract as round 1 answered it (bytes) | lean contract, the default now (bytes) | lean / full |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `object` | 184,917 | 322,947 | 12,167 | 3.8% |
| `field` | 64,335 | 88,770 | 21,015 | 23.7% |
| `permission` | 14,189 | 19,456 | 3,953 | 20.3% |
| `seed` | 6,916 | 9,570 | 3,898 | 40.7% |
| `view` | 369,244 | 745,321 | 21,981 (descriptions omitted, `truncated`) | 2.9% |
| `app` | 61,762 | 105,973 | 4,845 | 4.6% |
| `page` | 218,408 | 481,524 | 6,621 | 1.4% |
| `dashboard` | 18,735 | 36,914 | 4,125 | 11.2% |
| `report` | 14,481 | 28,094 | 4,696 | 16.7% |
| `dataset` | 11,133 | 19,858 | 3,671 | 18.5% |
| `action` | 48,946 | 79,733 | 15,041 | 18.9% |
| `flow` | 12,879 | 18,924 | 5,145 | 27.2% |
| `job` | 9,389 | 14,131 | 3,775 | 26.7% |
| `agent` | 6,688 | 11,257 | 4,353 | 38.7% |
| `skill` | 3,584 | 6,079 | 3,537 | 58.2% |
| `tool` | 2,856 | 4,509 | 3,053 | 67.7% |
| `translation` | 35,510 | 66,770 | 5,483 | 8.2% |

The skill table's other rows have no metadata type of their own in the served listing: a validation (inside `object`), an approval, a webhook and a knowledge source. `view` is the one type whose lean form needs the second rung: with descriptions it is over 24 KiB, so it answers its alternatives' keys without descriptions and says `truncated: true`; `contractPath: "/anyOf/2"` then answers that alternative's lean form with its descriptions (13,819 bytes).

Drills measured the same way:

| type | `contractPath` | answer | bytes |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| `object` | `/properties/fields` | lean, `truncated` | 717 |
| `object` | `/properties/fields/additionalProperties` | lean, `truncated` | 21,837 |
| `object` | `/properties/listViews` | lean, `truncated` | 652 |
| `view` | `/anyOf/0` | lean, `truncated` | 10,308 |
| `view` | `/anyOf/2` | lean, `truncated` | 13,819 |
| `page` | `/properties/regions` | lean, `truncated` | 591 |
| `app` | `/properties/navigation` | full | 252 |
| `object` | `/properties/nope` | refused `VALIDATION_ERROR 400` | n/a |

### `tools/list`, re-measured

Through the same path as round 1: `MCPServerRuntime.handleHttpRequest`, a `tools/list` round-trip on an authoring-only host with the `metadata:write` grant, serving the registry's tool definitions.

| Shape | `tools/list` response bytes | Delta vs main |
|:--|--:|--:|
| main (five tools) | 5,341 | — |
| round 1 head (`contract` flag, first description) | 5,526 | +185 |
| sixth tool `get_metadata_type_contract({ type })` (round 1 measurement) | 5,912 | +571 |
| this head: `contract` with its lean-form description, plus `contractPath` | **5,799** | **+458** |

The new `contractPath` property costs 209 bytes, and the `contract` description grew by 64 bytes to say what the lean form holds. The flag shape stays cheaper than the sixth tool.

### Pins changed in place

- The double's case "answers the entry's schema and seed beside the list": the default `contract` was `{ schema: FLOW_SCHEMA, createSeed }`; it is now `{ form: "lean", schema: LEAN_PROJECTION, createSeed }`, and `contractPath: ""` answers `{ form: "full", path: "", schema: FLOW_SCHEMA }`. Ruled by L1-a C1 and the seat's route (a).
- The app-crm flow-contract case: `contract.schema` was asserted equal to the `/meta/types` entry's schema; it now asserts the lean form's top-level keys and `required` equal the entry's, `required` still equals `getMetadataTypeSchema('flow')`'s, the seed is unchanged, and the root drill (`contractPath: ""`) answers the entry's schema whole. Same ruling.

## What changes

- **`list_metadata_items` takes an optional `contract: true`** (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts`). The reply then carries `contract` beside the list, read off the entry the protocol's `getMetaTypes` answers `GET /meta/types` with. That entry's schema is `getMetadataTypeSchema` through the protocol's one converter (`toJsonSchemaSafe`, with its hand-crafted fallback); the door adds no second converter and no second seed source. By default the contract is the lean form described in Round 2 above, a projection of that served schema.
- **`contractPath`** drills into the same served schema by JSON Pointer and answers the full sub-schema there, or its lean form marked `truncated` when over the cap.
- **`CONTRACT_REPLY_BYTE_CAP` (24 KiB)** bounds every contract in a reply.
- **No schema is said, never `{}`.** A live type whose entry carries no usable schema answers `{ schema: null, reason }`; a type the listing has no entry for answers the same shape with its own reason. A protocol with no `getMetaTypes` refuses the flagged call `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, as the door refuses every read it cannot serve.
- **Same gate as every other draft-door read.** It is the list read: the registry lists it only for a `metadata:write` token whose own user holds `manage_metadata`; the type-level read admission (`metaTypeReadRefusal`) refuses before any protocol read; an unknown type is refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST` by the list's own `refuseUnknownMetaListType`. Without the flag the reply is byte-for-byte as before.
- **`skills/objectstack-mcp-build/SKILL.md` section 3** now says: where you cannot read files, read the lean contract (`contract: true`), drill into your key with `contractPath`, and let the save check you. Same token count (1,226 of 1,226).

### Shape choice: the `tools/list` bytes (#34689 slimming kept)

Round 1's measurement chose the flag over a sixth tool (+185 against +571). Round 2's re-measurement is in the table above: +458 with `contractPath`, still below the sixth tool.

## Clause-② reading

Widening only. Every call a client could make before answers as before, except one read this PR itself added in round 1 (`contract: true`, unreleased), whose default answer is now the lean form. `contract` and `contractPath` are new optional inputs on a closed input schema (`additionalProperties: false`), so no call accepted today carried either: `contractPath` is a widening, and nothing accepted today is refused. A reply without `contract` is unchanged (pinned: the plain list's keys stay `type, count, items`). No save, publish, discard or other read changes.

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.test.ts`, `describe` "[#35761] list_metadata_items with contract: true…" (six cases, through the real `/mcp` domain and the real identity door): the lean form beside the list and the root drill answering the entry's schema whole, the plain reply unchanged; `contractPath` refused without `contract: true`, with `contract: false`, as a non-pointer and as a non-string, each before any protocol read, and on a type with no schema; the cap ladder on a wide schema (300 keys: descriptions dropped and `truncated`; 3,000 keys: `schema: null` with the over-cap reason), the reply under the cap in both; the no-schema shape for a schemaless entry and for an unlisted type; unknown type refused `INVALID_REQUEST 400` and a type the human may not read refused `PERMISSION_DENIED 403` before any protocol read; a user without `manage_metadata` lists nothing and is refused before the listing is read, while a data-only token and an API key are handed no registry at all.
- The app-crm block (real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` over SQLite, with the type registry the metadata plugin sets at boot):
  - `flow`, with no flow item stored: the lean form's keys and `required` equal the served entry's; `required` equals `z.toJSONSchema(getMetadataTypeSchema('flow'))`'s; `createSeed` equals `getMetadataCreateSeed('flow')`; `contractPath: ""` answers the entry's schema whole.
  - `object`, `view`, `page` and `app`: the lean contract is at most `CONTRACT_REPLY_BYTE_CAP` while the full served schema is over it, and it names every top-level key (or every union alternative) of the served schema.
  - `object` drilled at `/properties/fields`: lean and `truncated`, under the cap; its `drill` for `additionalProperties` is the next `contractPath`, answers under the cap, and names the served field schema's keys. `/properties/label` fits and answers the served sub-schema verbatim. `/properties/no_such_key` is refused `VALIDATION_ERROR 400`, the message naming the pointer and the `fields` key.

## Acceptance notes

- **Skill size readings.** `skills/objectstack-mcp-build/SKILL.md`: 94 lines before, 94 after; 1,226 tokens before, 1,226 after, against a ceiling of 1,226 (4,922 bytes before and after; the counter is bytes over four). The whole package is unchanged in tokens (285,577). The new wording was paid for inside the same paragraph: "Follow its pointers into `node_modules` only where" became "Follow its `node_modules` pointers where", and "Never write a key none of these shows" became "Write only keys these show". No ceiling moved.
- **Tier H at landing.** The diff touches `skills/**`, so landing needs an approval from an authorized approver.
- **The cap bounds the `contract`, not the whole reply.** The same reply carries the type's item list, whose size was never bounded on this door and is unchanged here.
- **`view` sits 2,595 bytes under the cap on the second rung.** If the `view` schema grows past that, the answer moves to the third rung (one descriptor per alternative, with descriptions), still under the cap, and the pin still holds.
- The served `object` and `view` schemas list stamped keys (`_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_provenance`, `_packageId` and others) among their properties; the lean form shows them because the served schema does. An observation about the converter's output, not changed here.
- The real `/meta/types` path also runs `translateMetaTypesResponse` (labels per locale). The contract answers schema and seed only, which that translation does not touch.

## Verification

Run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/mcp-authoring.test.ts`. Expect 50 passed, including the six "[#35761]" cases and the three "[#35761]" cases in the app-crm block.

Files to read first, by risk:
1. `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts`, `typeContractOf`, `fitContract`, `leanSchemaOf` and `resolveContractPath`: the lean form is a projection of the served schema, and no answer passes the cap.
2. `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.test.ts`, the new and changed `[#35761]` cases.
3. `skills/objectstack-mcp-build/SKILL.md`, section 3.
